title: Association between tumor-associated anemia and clinicopathological characteristics in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma – Influence of individual blood characteristics
summary: Anemia frequently occurs in patients with head and neck tumors. It can be caused by the tumor itself, malnutrition, bleeding, or cancer treatment. Previous studies suggest that anemia can influence the course of the disease and survival outcomes. Blood transfusions also appear to be linked to prognosis. However, it remains unclear which factors lead to a need for blood transfusions and what significance these factors have for the subsequent course of the disease. The aim of this study is therefore to investigate potential factors influencing the need for transfusion and to evaluate their significance for the prognosis of patients with head and neck tumors.
conditions: Malignant neoplasms of lip, oral cavity and pharynx
Malignant neoplasm of nasal cavity and middle ear
Malignant neoplasm of other and ill-defined sites: Head, face and neck

interventions.name: A retrospective analysis of patients diagnosed with a head and neck tumor between 2020 and 2026.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Head and neck tumor and extensive panendoscopy/laboratory workup
Exclusion criteria:
No head and neck tumor or no extensive panendoscopy workup
